This small village on the southern shore of Lake Izabal was once Guatemala's main port on the Pacific coast. The village attracts visitors with its exceptionally beautiful natural surroundings and the opportunity to take a rafting trip down the river that flows from the lake to the Pacific Ocean.

## Holidays at Lake Izabal

### Lake Izabal: a charming place for visitors!

Close to the village stands the well-preserved colonial San Felipe Fort, a national monument, along with the Mayan ruins of Quiriguá, which are on the UNESCO World Heritage List. The lake itself is famous as the only place in the world where freshwater sharks live. These are bull sharks that can reach 2.5–3 metres in length. Small cafés and restaurants along the lakeshore offer good places to eat.

At the shore of Lake Roca, mountains rise above the cold water and forest reaches down to the rocky shallows. This is one of the stops on a visit to Tierra del Fuego National Park near Ushuaia. The name Acigami is also used in tourist materials.

Walking trails through the park start at the lake. It is a pleasant place to linger by the water, take in the wooded slopes and watch the lake change colour beneath the clouds. A visit to the lake can be combined with Ensenada Zaratiegui and Lapataia bays.

Visitors travel to the Blue Lagoon from Barreirinhas through the sand dunes of Lençóis Maranhenses. Rainwater collects in the hollows between the dunes.

A walk beside the lagoon is combined with time to relax and swim. On the selected itinerary, travellers stay among the dunes until sunset before returning to town.

Lagoa da Conceição is particularly beautiful from above: a broad expanse of water opens up beyond the green slopes, houses line its shores, and farther away pale dunes lead towards the ocean side of the island. Then head down to the lagoon for a walk in the part of Florianópolis where life unfolds beside the water. Wide-open views sit alongside the small details of an old settlement.

The lagoon lies in the eastern part of Santa Catarina Island and gives its name to the surrounding district. Its history is connected to settlers who came to the island from the Azores. Hills, sand dunes and coastal vegetation create varied scenery within a single stop. The well-known beaches of the east coast are nearby, and visits to them can be combined with time at the lagoon.

On Ada Tours' 12-day journey through southern Brazil, Lagoa da Conceição is part of the Florianópolis sightseeing day, following a visit to the historic centre. It offers an opportunity to see the island beyond the city's squares and bridges. Allow separate time for a leisurely walk and photographs. Water activities, excursions in the surrounding area and beach visits are arranged according to the chosen itinerary.

Laguna Amarga is located in the area of Torres del Paine National Park. A stop at the water is part of driving itineraries through the park's lakes and mountain scenery.

Here, the open expanses of the Patagonian steppe meet the waters of the lagoon and the silhouettes of distant mountains. A visit to the lagoon is easy to combine with other viewpoints in the park.
